subject: Mutual action plan: performance synthesis and close timeline
messages:
From: Sam Khan <sam.khan@medlink.com>
To: Olg a Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medlink.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: interest in Redwood for clinical triage (MAP request)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — MedLink is keen to move towards a pilot. Our security and procurement teams asked for a concrete mutual action plan that includes a performance evaluation (latency, throughput, TTFT, concurrency) because our triage flows are latency-sensitive during peak hours.

Can you share a recommended MAP + a test plan we can run against our representative workload (avg prompt len ~120 tokens, peaks to 400 tokens, ~3k QPS burst across the service)? Ideally we'd like results on at least three model variants so we can weigh quality vs cost.

Target close timeline: procurement would like contract terms finalized by 2027-09-30 if the pilot outcomes look good.

Best,
Sam
Sr. Product Manager — MedLink
[MedLink logo]
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Khan <sam.khan@medlink.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: interest in Redwood for clinical triage (MAP request)

Sam — thanks, and great to hear the team is moving toward a pilot. Attaching a draft MAP and an evaluation plan we use for latency/throughput gating. High level plan below; full MAP attached as MedLink_MAP_v2.xlsx.

Summary (short):
- Evaluation goals: p95 latency <= 350ms, TTFT <= 120ms, stable throughput >= 1.2k tokens/sec at baseline concurrency 16, graceful degradation to 32 concurrent streams.
- Variants to test (catalog names): rwd-7b-q4, rwd-13b-fp16, rwd-70b-8bit. We recommend starting with 7b-q4 for cost-sensitive flows and 13b-fp16 for the highest quality/latency trade-off.
- Workload: 10k sample requests (mix reflecting your prompt length distribution), three ramp profiles (steady, 5-min burst, long tail).
- Acceptance criteria: quality regression <= 2.5% vs baseline (MedLink reference eval set), no sustained queueing beyond 2s, fallbacks defined.
- Timeline: quick pilot (2 weeks), then decision window to close by 2027-09-30.

Attachments: MedLink_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP + responsibilities), benchmark_results.csv (we'll populate after run), rwd_variant_summary.pdf (variant notes).

I'll coordinate the test harness and provide prebuilt k6/JMeter scripts and a small Redwood runner config you can execute against our hosted eval endpoints. Karthik/Marissa — can you confirm capacity for the burst runs next Tuesday and that we can reserve the dedicated test pool?

— Olga
Olga Petrov | Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sam Khan <sam.khan@medlink.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: interest in Redwood for clinical triage (MAP request)

Looping in some quick capacity/tech detail. We can provision a temporary dedicated pool for the pilot with the following baseline nodes: 4x A100-class GPUs for the 13b-fp16 baseline, and an alternative 2x A100 pool for the 7b-q4 runs. Preliminary notes on expected performance (lab runs with MedLink sample corpus):

- rwd-7b-q4 (quantized)
  - median latency (single stream, 120 tokens): 72 ms TTFT, p95 generation latency: 210 ms
  - throughput (tokens/sec, continuous): 1,400 tokens/sec at concurrency 16; sustained to 2,600 tokens/sec in throughput-only tests (careful: higher tail latency under burst).
  - quality: reference accuracy on EMR extraction set: 86.2% (our baseline for quick triage tasks)

- rwd-13b-fp16
  - TTFT: 95 ms, p95 latency: 310 ms
  - throughput: 1,200 tokens/sec at concurrency 16; recommended for flows that need better QA accuracy
  - quality: EMR extraction accuracy: 91.7%

- rwd-70b-8bit
  - TTFT: 160 ms, p95 latency: 540 ms
  - throughput: 900 tokens/sec at concurrency 16; robust on long-context prompts but higher cost
  - quality: EMR extraction accuracy: 94.6%

Notes on TTFT (time-to-first-token): measurement includes network hop to the hosted pool and model startup/kv-warm path. Our pilot harness will report both cold and warmed TTFT (we recommend warmed runs for production gating).

I'll upload the full CSV of detailed runs to the shared Drive after today's internal replay. Marissa — can you confirm if we should run an additional quantized 13b variant (13b-q4) for a middle-ground?

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: benchmark_results.csv]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Sam Khan <sam.khan@medlink.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: interest in Redwood for clinical triage (MAP request)

Thanks — quick clarifications and an action item list for the MAP.

Clarifications:
- The MedLink sample burst profile (3k QPS for 45s) will be reproducible in our test pool; we'll run three independent burst tests and capture full token-level latency and queue length metrics.
- For acceptance, Sam — can your engineering lead confirm whether p95 latency <= 350ms is a hard SLO or a preferred target? That will change which variant we recommend for pilot.

Action items (who/when):
- MedLink: share the ground truth eval set & a subset of production prompts (anonymized) — due Mon 2027-09-13 (Sam)
- Redwood: run baseline warmed and cold runs across rwd-7b-q4, rwd-13b-fp16, rwd-13b-q4 (Karthik) — results by Tue 2027-09-14
- Procurement/Legal: share contract template and any SOC2/KMS requirements (Sam/procurement) — target 2027-09-16
- Redwood Sales: draft pilot statement of work & pricing (Olga) — draft by 2027-09-14

Tentative recommendation: start pilot on rwd-13b-fp16 if MedLink prioritizes quality; start on rwd-7b-q4 if cost and lower latency are primary. We'll capture regression vs your reference set and include fallback routes in the MAP (auto-route to smaller model under heavy load).

Regards,
Marissa Cole | Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rwd_variant_summary.pdf]
From: Sam Khan <sam.khan@medlink.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: interest in Redwood for clinical triage (MAP request)

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the detail — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick answers and one ask:

- p95 <= 350ms is a hard SLO for our primary triage path; fallback to a degraded path (lower quality but <200ms) is acceptable for non-critical screens.
- We'll deliver the anonymized eval set on Monday (2027-09-13).
- Ask: can you include estimated monthly cost delta for starting pilot on each variant (per 200k tokens/day baseline)? That'll help procurement.

If the pilot matches the SLOs and quality, procurement will accelerate to hit the 2027-09-30 close. Looking forward to the CSV and the MAP workbook.

— Sam
Sr. Product Manager — MedLink
[Procurement: procurement@medlink.com]
